evaluations.model_answer:
(It is observed in the figure that the path length of the mediating network reaches a local maximum at the B1 level (about 3.42) and then declines at the B2 level. What linguistic phenomenon does this B1-to-B2 downward trend reflect?)

This B1 to B2 decline likely reflects the increasing specialization of vocabulary knowledge. At the B1 level, learners tend to have a somewhat more general vocabulary base. As they progress to B2, they develop more specialized vocabulary and the connections within their network become more refined and localized (i.e., less "average path length" because they navigate their specialized vocabulary efficiently).  In simple terms, their knowledge becomes more targeted, reducing the need for lengthy detours through less relevant words.
